title: Reject unknown users when adding a tenant member and count only real owners
goal: AddMember validates only that the tenant exists (tenant_service.go:858-903), and tenant_memberships has no foreign key to system_user (000013_tenant_canary.up.sql:48-59). Any id — a typo, a deleted user, a user from another tenant — becomes a member row. Worse, a row with role=owner for a nonexistent user is counted by ensureNotLastOwner (tenant_service.go:948-975), so the real last owner can be removed, leaving the tenant with an owner that can never log in. This wave makes the write path honest: the user must exist and not be deleted, the last-owner count must join system_user, and the console must stop asking operators to type a numeric id. It deliberately does not decide whether cross-tenant membership is allowed; that is W3/W4. The test fixtures currently add ids that do not exist, which encoded the defect; they must be updated to create real users rather than relaxing the new check.
findings: TC-03 (P2): AddMember has no user-existence check, and the suite confirms it by construction: every tenant test writes membership rows for user ids that have no system_user row. Measured call sites on 2026-10-27: tenant_service_test.go uses 100 (8 calls) and 200+i (loop); tenant_lifecycle_guard_test.go uses 100, 101, 102, 201 and 777; tenant_handler_test.go uses 101-103 and 88001. All three files pass today (119 tests green), which is the proof that the check does not exist.

TC-03 (P2): ensureNotLastOwner counts tenant_memberships rows with role=owner and status=active without joining system_user, so a phantom owner row satisfies the invariant and permits removing the real owner. The owner guard itself works for real rows — TestRemoveMemberRefusesLastOwner passes — the gap is only who is counted.
TC-03 usability: TenantList.tsx:847-856 asks for a raw numeric user id, making the phantom path a realistic operator error rather than an API-only scenario.

Ordering constraint already pinned by a test: TestDeletedTenantRefusesNewMembers (tenant_lifecycle_guard_test.go:210-224) expects ErrTenantNotFound for a tombstone, so the tenant-existence check must stay ahead of the new user check.

in: AddMember validates that user_id identifies a live system_user row (deleted_at IS NULL) before writing the membership; keep the tenant-existence check first so a tombstone still returns ErrTenantNotFound
Return the existing user-not-found error contract (user.batch.not_found or an equivalent registered key) and map it in tenant_platform_handler.go
ensureNotLastOwner counts owners through system_user, requiring the user row to be undeleted and enabled

Update every tenant test fixture that adds a nonexistent user, instead of lowering the new validation: tenant_service_test.go (100, 200+i), tenant_lifecycle_guard_test.go (100, 101, 102, 201, 777) and tenant_handler_test.go (101-103, 88001). Add one shared helper that creates the system_user rows so each test states ids it owns

Add regressions: unknown user id is rejected; a phantom owner row does not prevent removing the real last owner from being blocked; removing the real last owner still fails while a second real owner exists

Replace the free-text user id field in the tenant member dialog with a tenant-scoped user selector (existing users fetched with the current X-Tenant-Id scope, excluding users already active in this tenant), keeping the membership-role select
Show a clear empty state when the tenant has no addable users
out: Deciding or implementing cross-tenant membership policy (W3/W4)
Mapping the membership role (owner/admin/member) to an IAM role
Changing the membership table schema or adding a foreign key
Changing RemoveMember semantics beyond the owner count
Deleting the existing AddMember tests instead of fixing their fixtures
Adding a platform-wide user search to the member dialog

implementationNotes: Order of checks matters: tenant first, then user, so the tombstone regression keeps returning ErrTenantNotFound and does not leak whether a user id exists.
Use a scoped query consistent with the rest of the tenant service; do not introduce a raw unscoped lookup just to satisfy the check.
The owner count joins system_user. Check the test database DDL in tenant_service_test.go: it creates system_user, so the join works; the fixtures simply never inserted rows.
A disabled (status != 1) user is not a live owner. Keep the add path permissive about status if the existing behaviour depends on it, but exclude disabled and deleted users from the owner count.
The member selector must reuse the existing user-list API and the X-Tenant-Id request scope; do not add a new endpoint for it.
If the selector cannot paginate cleanly, cap it at the first bounded page and say so in one comment; do not build a new search service.
This wave must land before W4 so that W4 can assume every membership row points at a real user.

tenant_handler_test.go is deleted by W8. If W8 lands first, ignore it here; if this wave lands first, patch its two AddMember calls as part of the fixture update so the file is not left red in between. Do not delete the file here.
Run with PANTHEON_TEST_DSN set. Without it 85 tenant tests skip and the package reports ok in 0.04s, so a missed fixture would look green.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Update the fixtures first so the suite expresses real users, then add the failing phantom-owner test, then fix the service and the UI.
reviewerPosture: Confirm every test id now maps to a real system_user row.
Confirm a phantom owner row no longer satisfies the last-owner invariant.
Confirm AddMember still returns ErrTenantNotFound for a tombstone before reaching the user check.
Confirm the member dialog no longer accepts free-text ids and sends the selected user id.
Confirm no new endpoint or dependency was added.
